catalog_locator: Ch. 4 'Prosodies, système vocalique et tons', sec. 4.4 'Les tons' and 4.4.1 'Inventaire des tons', p.117; sec. 4.4.2 p.118; sec. 5.1.1 p.125 for the syllable remark.
catalog_quote: Le cuvok présente un système tonal à deux tons, haut et bas. Pour une bonne compréhension de son système tonal, il faut faire les remarques suivantes: a. Le ton de la voyelle épenthétique est toujours bas. Par conséquent les réalisations [i] et [u] ont aussi toujours un ton bas. b. Le ton de la syllabe à voyelle allongée est toujours [HB] c. Les radicaux verbaux portent toujours un ton bas sur leur voyelle. d. Le système nominal ne montre pas un grand nombre d’oppositions contrastives car très peu de paires minimales ont été identifiées. [...] Le cuvok possède deux tons phonémiques: le ton bas (B) et le ton haut (H). Le ton joue un rôle d’égale importance tant au niveau lexical que grammatical. Les deux tons peuvent se trouver dans toutes les catégories grammaticales, sauf pour le fait que le ton haut n’apparait pas dans les radicaux verbaux. Il existe très peu de paires minimales et nous en donnons quelques exemples des tons contrastifs en (51). [...] Il faudra cependant remarquer que, dans les noms, contrairement aux radicaux verbaux, le ton n’est pas prévisible.
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.translation: Cuvok has a tonal system with two tones, high and low. For a good understanding of its tonal system the following remarks are needed: a. the tone of the epenthetic vowel is always low [...] b. the tone of a syllable with a lengthened vowel is always [HL]; c. verb roots always carry a low tone on their vowel. [...] Cuvok has two phonemic tones: low (B) and high (H). Tone plays an equally important role at the lexical and the grammatical level. [...] It must be noted, however, that in nouns, unlike verb roots, tone is not predictable.
new_statements.citation: Ndokobaï, Dadak. 2021. Grammaire cuvok: langue tchadique centrale du Cameroun. PhD dissertation, Universiteit Leiden (hdl:1887/3185511).

new_statements.rule_in_words: Cuvok is described as a two-tone language (H, L) with lexical and grammatical tone; verb roots are all-L, noun melodies are lexical (mostly all-L or HL), epenthetic schwa is always L. The grammar's phonology chapters make no statement at all about word stress or accent, and the author treats the syllable as not a relevant unit.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress; tonal remarks only (epenthetic vowel always L; long-vowel syllable always HL; high-toned má- prefix on most polysyllabic nouns).
new_statements.domain_note: Tone described on words in citation form (phonetic transcriptions with both tone levels marked); intonation mentioned only for polar questions (sec. 7.1.3, p.201). No word-stress domain discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: Ndokobai 2021 describes Cuvok as spoken around Tchouvok (Mayo-Tsanaga, Far North Cameroon); the author (native speaker) states the language is homogeneous with no dialectal varieties (p.7). Matches cuvo1236 exactly.

new_statements.quote: 3.13 Ton On ne marque pas le ton sur les mots en tchouvok. Il y a très peu de paires de mots où le ton seul sert à distinguer les mots, et dans de tels cas le contexte peut normalement éclaircir le sens.
new_statements.translation: 3.13 Tone. Tone is not marked on words in Tchouvok. There are very few pairs of words where tone alone serves to distinguish the words, and in such cases the context can normally clarify the meaning.

new_statements.relation_note: Compatible with the existing Ndokobaï 2021 statement (two-tone system H/B, no stress statement): both describe Cuvok as tonal with nothing on stress. Adds the detail that tone has a very low functional load at the word level (very few minimal pairs) and is not. It does not supply a stress rule, so the catalog's empty rule field stays empty.
new_statements.rule_in_words: An orthography sketch, not a phonology: it treats tone as existing but of very low functional load (very few tone-only minimal pairs) and leaves it unwritten. It says nothing about word stress, accent or prominence (a full-text search for stress/accent|stress|toniqu|proémin over the whole text: no hits). Intro (p.2) states the sketch rests on the phonological study by 'Ndokabaï Gaston (2003)', i.e. work 1.
new_statements.exceptions: none on stress; tone: 'very few' tone-only minimal pairs, otherwise disambiguated by context
new_statements.identity_note: Both works concern the same language (Cuvok = Tchouvok, ISO cuv), spoken around Zamaï, Mayo-Tsanaga, Far North Cameroon; the Gravina sketch is a community orthography document for the whole language, with a text told by Amadou Ruben, not a dialect-specific description. 'Ndokabaï Gaston (2003)' in Gravina's intro is the same person as Ndokobaï Dadak (author of the 2003 mémoire and the 2021 Leiden grammar).

new_statements.quote: Notre investigation a permis d’identifier deux tons ponctuels dans la langue cuvok. Ce sont principalement le ton bas et le ton haut. Par définition, un ton ponctuel est celui dont la hauteur musicale de la voix reste constante au cours de son émission sur la syllabe qui le porte. Notre langue d’étude possède deux niveaux de tons ponctuels : le niveau haut et le niveau bas. [...] (p.35) A la fin de cette partie, nous avons pu répertorier deux tons tous lexicaux car nous n’avons pas enregistré des cas où un mot change de classe grammaticale à cause d’une syllabe qui change du registre tonal.
new_statements.translation: Our investigation identified two level tones in the Cuvok language. These are principally the low tone and the high tone. By definition, a level tone is one whose musical pitch stays constant during its production on the syllable that carries it. Our language of study has two level-tone registers: high and low. [...] (p.35) At the end of this part, we have recorded two tones, both lexical, since we found no cases where a word changes grammatical class because a syllable changes tonal register.
new_statements.citation: Ndokobaï, Dadak (2003). Etude phonologique du Cuvok et principes orthographiques. Yaoundé: Université de Yaoundé. Universite de Yaounde I. 151 pp.

new_statements.relation_note: Same type as the existing statement from Ndokobaï 2021 (two-tone system H/L, no stress statement); the catalog record itself has an empty rule. The 2003 thesis adds the full inventory of tone patterns on polysyllables and the tone-marking orthography decision but nothing on stress, so it does not change the catalog reading.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Cuvok is analysed as a tone language with two level tonemes, H and L, both lexical (minimal pairs sec. 3.4.1, p.34); ch.8 'Les schémas tonals' (pp.89-91) lists all H/L combinations on 2-, 3- and 4-syllable words with no restriction stated; the orthography (9.2.4 p.99, 10.2.1 p.103) marks H only. Nowhere does the thesis speak of word stress or accent in Cuvok. The only 'accent' discussion is the ch.2 literature review (pp.25-26) reporting Roberts 2001 / Barreteau 1995 / Wolff 1987 on whether Central Chadic languages are tonal at all or accentual ('Roberts (2001) montre aussi que le Mukulu (Tchad) devrait être considéré comme une langue à accents'), which the author does not apply to Cuvok; for Cuvok he concludes two tonemes.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. On tone: syllabic consonants can bear tone (sec. 3.1 p.32, [ɮə̀ɓà] 'forgeron'); author says functional load of tone is low in Central Chadic and that a later morphological study might reveal further tonal behaviour (p.35).
new_statements.identity_note: Ndokobaï 2003 describes Cuvok (ALCAM 181, Mafa group, Central Chadic) as spoken by the Tchouvok people, arrondissement de Mokolo, Mayo-Tsanaga, Far North Cameroon; sec. 9.1.3 p.97 quotes a survey that 'The Cuvok language is definitely homogeneous without dialect'. Matches cuvo1236 exactly; the author is a native speaker.

sources.note: Nothing. Ch.3 (consonants, pp.69-94) and ch.4 (prosodies, vowels, tones, pp.95-124) describe a palatalization prosody, a two-vowel system with epenthetic schwa, and a two-tone system (H, L: sec. 4.4, pp.117-124; verb roots always L, noun tone lexical/unpredictable, epenthetic vowel always L, long-vowel syllable always HL). No mention of accent/stress anywhere in the body text (a full-text search for stress/accent/stress/tonique/proéminence nil); author also states the syllable is not a relevant unit in Cuvok (p.125).
